heading: Asian Games 2026 Highlights: Elavenil Valarivan claims 2nd silver medal; Suchika Tariyal confirms MMA medal
paragraphs: Elavenil Valarivan has ensured India have started Sunday at the Asian Games 2026 in Nagoya with two silver medals. First, the rifle shooter teamed up with Sonam Uttam Maskar and Vidarsa K Vinod to claim a team silver in the women’s 10m air rifle team event. Then, she returned to the air rifle ranges to claim an individual silver as well. Meanwhile, Suchika Tariyal has also confirmed a medal after she entered the semi-finals of women’s traditional 60kg in the mixed martial arts event.

Quimcy Dsouza endured a double heartbreak after ending fourth in the women’s singles and the mixed doubles event in teqball. The Mumbai girl first lost the bronze medal playoff to Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto in women’s singles, and then lost in the mixed doubles bronze medal playoff with Mohd Anas Imran Beg to a Vietnamese pairing.

Shooting (MEDAL ALERT): Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Uttam Maskar, and Vidarsa K Vinod have claimed a team silver medal in the 10m Air Rifle Women’s team event and could also add to that tally in the individual event
Shooting (MEDAL ALERT): Elavenil Valarivan won an individual silver medal in the 10m Air Rifle Women’s event. She was leading for most of the final, but ceded the top spot in the final few shots.
MMA (CONFIRMED MEDAL ALERT): Suchika Tariyal confirms India’s a medal in MMA after entering semis of women’s traditional 60kg in MMA event

Cricket (CONFIRMED MEDAL ALERT): India’s women’s cricket team defeated Bangladesh by 114 runs in the semi-finals to book a clash with Sri Lanka to defend their gold medal from the Hangzhou 2023 Games.
Hockey: Indian women’s team thump Uzbekistan 19-0 in group stage match
Hockey: Indian men’s team beat Indonesia 13-1 in group stage match
Teqball: Quimcy Dsouza loses to Yuina Sakamoto in bronze medal playoff to end fourth
Teqball: Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza and Mohd Anas Imran Beg lost to Minh Tan Nguyen and Gia Nghi Trinh (Vietnam) in bronze medal playoff

Today was all about the shooters, Elavenil Valarivan in particular. Our man on the ground Mihir Vasavda says that they had undergone a bus journey of 2 hours just to get to the venue. Now this is Japan, the roads are smooth, the bus comfortable and the route scenic and yet, staying mentally and physically fresh is never easy in these circumstances. Tomorrow Himanshu Dhillon, Parth Mane and Rudrankksh Patil will be in action in the men's 10m air rifle individual as well team finals. All eyes will also be on Suchika Tariyal in the 60kg MMA final. Many, many more big events will be there of course and we will be getting a comprehensive schedule out for you soon. Join us tomorro morning. Ciao!

It's a 3-0 defeat for the Indian men's team against Iran in group F. Harmeet took the match all the way and lost to Alamian 3-2. Both the men's and women's teams face Pakistan in their next matches tomorrow.

India are facing Iran in men's team group F and trail 2-0. Thus far, things haven't quite gone their way. Manush Shah was blanked 3-0 by Noshad Alamiyan in the first match after which Manav Thakkar lost 3-0 to Benyamin Faraji. Harmeet Desai is in action now and he is facing Nima Alamian.
The edge of a coin is barely there. A thin, almost invisible sliver. That was Elavenil Valarivan’s (pronounced Il_a-vennil Val_a-rivan) distance from Asian Games gold on Sunday.

At the end of a thrilling final, in which she led for all but the last two shots, Elavenil needed to score 0.6 more than Japan’s Taichi Hinata. She shot 10.1 and finished on 252.4. Hinata had 253.0. For all the years Elavenil has spent waiting for a big medal at a major Games, it came down to this tiny sliver.
Her first thought after the final shot? “Oh, 0.6. Okay…” her voice trails off.

Elavenil’s career has often been about being close — close enough to be called India’s next big shooting star, close enough to be ranked No. 1 in the world, close enough to watch others move ahead while she waited for her moment. Read more from Mihir Vasavda HERE.

And now Yashaswini Ghorpade has won her match 3-2 and India take the tie by the same scoreline as well. Yashaswini had earlier won the first match she had played as well, and that was against Jian Zeng 3-1. Seeeja Akula then lost 3-2 to Ming Loy and Diya Chitale then lost to Zao Tan 3-1. However, Sreeja and Yashaswini both amends in the fourth and fifth matches and India prevail.

India are alive in their women's team Group F tie against Singapore thanks to a remarkable comeback by Sreeja Akula. She had lost the first game but went on to charge to victory in the next three to win 3-1. It is all square at 2-2 between the two teams as we go into match 3 between Yashaswini Ghorpade and Ming Loy

The Indian women's team have steamrolled Bangladesh in the semifinal and booked a place for themselves in the final. This means that they are assured of at least a silver, India are the defending gold medallists remember. Shafali Verma's unbeaten 100 in 49 balls helped India set a target of 196. Bangladesh were all out for just 81 in 15.4 overs, with Nandani Sharma and Deepti Sharma taking three wickets each and Shree Charani picking two.

The Indian Men's Hockey Team launched its campaign at the 20th Asian Games with a dominant 13-1 victory over Indonesia in a Pool A fixture at the Kawasaki Juko Stadium on Sunday. Eight different goal-scorers were on target for the Indian team, headlined by Dilpreet Singh's four-goal haul, as India put on a clinical display from the first whistle to the last, announcing their intent as they begin the defence of their continental crown.

Elavenil Valarivan (born 2 August 1999) is an Indian rifle shooter from Tamil Nadu, currently based in Gujarat, specializing in the 10m Air Rifle event. She began competitive shooting in 2014 and trains under personal coach Neha Chavan, with Deepali Deshpande and Deepak Dubey serving as her national coaches.

A two-time Olympian, Elavenil represented India at the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games and has consistently ranked among the world's leading women's air rifle shooters, reaching World No. 1 during her career. Elavenil rose to international prominence after winning the gold medal at the 2018 ISSF Junior World Cup in Sydney in only her second ISSF competition, setting a Junior World Qualification Record. She has since won multiple medals at the ISSF World Championships, ISSF World Cups, ISSF World Cup Final, and Asian Championships, establishing herself as one of India's most decorated air rifle athletes.
On Sunday, Elavenil won two medals at the Asian Games, both silvers. Those two medals adds to a jawdroppingly long list of medals at various events:
Silver – 10m Air Rifle Women Junior, ISSF World Championships, Changwon, Republic of Korea (2018)
Bronze – 10m Air Rifle Women Team, ISSF World Championships, Cairo, Egypt (2022)
Bronze – 10m Air Rifle Women, ISSF World Championships, Cairo, Egypt (2025)
Gold – 10m Air Rifle Women, ISSF World Cup, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (2019)
Gold – 10m Air Rifle Women, ISSF World Cup, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (2023)
Bronze – 10m Air Rifle Women, ISSF World Cup, Munich, Germany (2025)
Gold – 10m Air Rifle Women, Asian Championships, New Delhi, India (2026)
Gold – 10m Air Rifle Women, Asian Championships, Shymkent, Kazakhstan (2025)

Indian shuttlers are into the Quarterfinals of the women's team event! PV Sindhu and Co cruised past Kazakhstan 3-0 in the Round of 16 to enter the quarterfinals. India will now face Japan on 22nd September to secure a medal in the Women's Team event.
WS1: Pusarla V Sindhu bt. Kamila Smagulova 21-7, 21-9
India made a flying start to their shooting campaign at the 20th Asian Games, securing two silver medals on the opening day of competition at the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery.
Olympian Elavenil Valarivan clinched the silver medal in the Women's 10m Air Rifle individual final.
Meanwhile the trio of Elavenil, Sonam Uttam Maskar and Vidarsa Kochalumkal Vinod combined to win the team silver.

In an impressive individual final, Elavenil produced consistent high-10s to shoot a total of 252.4. She pushed the contest to the final shot, finishing just 0.6 points behind Japan's Hinata Taichi, who took the gold medal with a new Asian Games record of 253.0. South Korea's Olympic champion Ban Hyojin took the bronze medal with a score of 230.4.
India's Sonam Uttam Maskar also featured in the eight-woman final, finishing sixth with an elimination score of 167.0.

Earlier in the day, the Indian contingent opened the nation's medal account at the Games through the team event, which is decided by aggregate qualification scores. India posted a combined total of 1898.0 to secure second place on the podium.

Sonam led the qualifying effort for India with an outstanding 634.1 to finish third, while Elavenil qualified in seventh place with 633.5. Vidarsa added a solid score of 630.4 to place 12th in the individual rankings and seal the team silver for India.

China took the team gold medal with a total of 1904.2, led by qualification leader Wang Zifei (636.8), Han Jiayu (633.8) and Du Yuchen (633.6). Hosts Japan claimed the team bronze medal with an aggregate of 1897.1.

Shooting action continues on Monday, 21 September 2026, with medals on offer in the Men's 10m Air Rifle individual and team competitions. The opening day of qualification for both the Men's and Women's Skeet events will also get under way at the range.
That's just 15 points conceded. Sindhu ceded 16 and Unnati 17.
Kazakhstan are not a strong team at all in badminton. But this was a good workout to understand the court conditions ahead of Japan.

India's men's and women's teams began their table tennis campaigns at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with identical 3-0 wins over Indonesia in their respective Group F openers on Sunday, reports Press Trust of India.
The women's team got their campaign off to a winning start as Sreeja Akula, Diya Chitale and Yashaswini Ghorpade swept their Indonesian opponents.
Sreeja beat Ni Maharani 3-1 in the opening rubber, recovering from an 8-11 second-game loss to win 11-3, 11-4, 11-4.
Diya then defeated Almaira Nebuchadnezzar 3-0 (11-9, 11-8, 11-5) before Yashaswini sealed the tie with a 3-0 (12-10, 11-4, 11-4) win over Citra Rasmi.
The men followed with an equally dominant 3-0 victory, though they were pushed harder in the second rubber.
Sathiyan Gnanasekaran put India ahead with a 3-0 win over Muhammad Negara, prevailing 11-8, 11-7, 11-9.
Manav Thakkar then survived a five-game battle against Muhammad Junindra, winning 3-2. Manav took the first game 11-7, dropped the second 8-11, and regained the lead by winning the third 11-6.
Junindra forced a decider by taking the fourth 11-6, but Manav held his nerve to win the fifth 11-9.
Manush Shah completed the men's sweep with a 3-0 win over Affan Pratama, prevailing 11-9, 11-9, 12-10.
India's women are grouped alongside Indonesia, Pakistan and Singapore in Group F.
The men's team are clubbed with Iran, Pakistan and Indonesia.

Like the women's team earlier today, the Indian men's hockey team's goal tally for this match has gone into double digits. Sukhjeet Singh scored the 10th goal and now Jugraj Singh has scored India's 11th with a rasping dragflick from a PC.

Tanvi Sharma now in action for India, and she is facing Diana Namenova. It is not much or a surprise that she absolutely dominated the first game. Tanvi won it 21-5 but Namenova has managed to stay with the Indian in the early stages of the second game. Tanvi leads 4-2.

We are into the third quarter in the Indian men's hockey team's opening match of these Games against Indonesia and the former are leading 7-1. Indonesia just scored their first goal through a penalty corner in what has thus far been one-way traffic otherwise.
On coaches bench - Pullela Gopichand & Irwansyah both.
One more win needed to secure a likely quarterfinal clash vs Japan

The Indian women's team made a thunderous start to their Asian Games 2026 campaign, overwhelming Uzbekistan 19-0 in their opening Pool B encounter in Kakamigahara on Saturday. The victory was headlined by a remarkable eight-goal outing from penalty-corner specialist Deepika, while Ishika completed a hat-trick as India produced an attacking masterclass from start to finish. Eight different Indian players found the net in a dominant display, as the match also saw veteran goalkeeper Savita reach a significant personal milestone.

A silver medal and some heartbreak for Elavenil Valarivan! She claims her 2nd silver medal of the day, but she would not be very happy with that. She was leading the event for so long, but in the final shots, she was overtaken by the eventual gold medallist from Japan, Hinata Taichi.
A 0.6 difference between Elavenil and the gold medal winning Japanese shooter at the end after 24 shots!
Fine margins and all that! Just look at the gap at the top. Just 0.2!
Shivani Naik with a lament: 4 TV channels dedicated to Asian Games. 3 showing cricket. No badminton. Yet.
Elavenil Valarivan confirms India's second medal on a day she also played a role in India's first -- a team silver in the 10m air rifle event.
Elavenil is in contention for gold at the moment with just two more shooters left in the fray at the moment.

This is the first time there will be no Chinese shooter on a 10m Air rifle podium at the Asian Games. Last time such an instance happened 40 years back in the 1986 Seoul Asian Games when this discipline was introduced at the showpiece. This will also mean that after 2014, the first time a non Chinese will win the gold medal.

Elavenil is still hanging on to top spot, she could be India's first gold medallist at teh Asian Games in Nagoya! A few shots remain in her way to the top step of the podium. here are the standings after 17 shots.

Elavenil Valarivan holds on to her lead after 15 shots while Sonam was bearing down on a bronze in fourth spot but slips to fifth. Nobata was decimal points away from Ela at one point, but falls to third then rises to second!
Elavenil Valarivan leads after 12 shots while Sonam is bearing down on a bronze is currently fourth.
MMA fighter Varun Sanyal declared unfit, ends his campaign at Asian Games.

Indian coach Pooja Ghatkar. Blast from the past. She missed qualification for Rio Olympics by a slightest whisker. Ayonika Paul went through at the Delhi qualis. India has a long long history in women's air rifle starting with troika of Anjali, Deepali and Suma. But women's air rifle has not managed to breakthrough at Olympics. The Chinese tend to be the problem to nail down a gold. Gold - no less. But let's see how this goes.
Elavenil Valarivan and Sonam Uttam Maskar are the shooters in the fray for an individual medal in the 10m air rifle event after teaming up for a silver medal in the team event.
Here we go! After the Indian rifle shooters won a team event silver, they are back in the individual 10m final contending for another medal.
Mihir Vasavda, who is in the shooting hall at Nagoya, writes:

Packed finals hall. Lots of Koreans — perhaps more than the locals, going by the loud cheers for the Korean shooters. China’s Han Jiayu, a favourite for gold, gets the centre target; flanked by the two Indians. Sonam on her left, Elavenil on right

Nine series of 106.0 and more. That’s what led to the world record of 1904.2 by the gold medal wining Chinese trio of Wang Ziefei, Han Jiayu and Du Yechen to win the women’s 10m air rifle team gold. Ziefei had four series out of six series in excess of 106.0 with her fourth series score of 106.9 being the highest shot by any shooter in the qualification.
Youngster Sonam Maskar rose to the occasion and finished fourth in a very competitive qualification with 634.1 points.

Experienced Elavenil Valarivan had a qualification of two halves. She was supreme in the first three series scoring 318.3 and was the only match to qualification winner Wang Zifei of China. However, she went off rails in the second half finishing with 315.2 in the last three series including the lowest score of 104.7.
Vidarsa Vinod K who is more of a 50m 3P expert scored a good 630.5 but given the standard of qualification, she can only finish 12th.

In Hangzhou Asian Games, Chinese trio of Jiayu Han (634.1), Yuting Huang (631.6) and Zhilin Wang (630.9) had won the women’s 10m air rifle team gold with a cumulative score of 1896.6 while the Indian trio of Ranita Jindal (631.9), Mehul Ghosh (630.8) and Ashi Chouksey (623.2) had won the silver with a cumulative score of 1886 points.

India have won their first medal at the 2026 Asian Games, and expectedly its the shooters who deliver the medal! At the last Asian Games, our shooters had won 22 medals for India to push them to the triple-digit medal mark.
The trio of Sonam Maskar, Elavenil Valarivan and Vidarsa Vinod K opened India's medal account with a silver medal in the women's 10m Air rifle event.
While China took the gold medal with a total score of 1904.2, India held on to second spot by 0.9 as Japan finished third with 1897.1.

China’s cumulative total of 1904.2 in the women’s 10m air rifle is a new world record. The Chinese trio of Wang Ziefei, Han Jiayu and Du Du Yechen surpassed the earlier world record score of 1902.0 shot by Chinese trio of Liu Yafei, Peng Xinlu and Zhang Liyuan in last year’s Asian Championships.

India in all likelihood has won the first medal of the Asian Games and it has come in the women's 10m Air rifle team event. The Indian team is set to finish second behind China who created the World Record with a score of 1904.2 while India's cumulative score is 1898. The Korean shooter needs 75.5 in the last seven shots which looks tough at the moment.
India on course to a team silver in 10m women’s rifle. The combined total of 3 shooters is 1898. China is ahead by a mile. India keeping the Koreans at bay.
India have taken a 19-0 lead against Uzbekistan in the pool B clash with six minutes left in the match! Deepika has scored 8 goals!
The Uzbekistan goalkeeper enduring the suffering is a 16-year-old.
Elavenil Valarivan shoots a final series of 105.4 and ends with a final score of 105.4. She is placed seventh and expected to maintain her spot.

Elavenil Valarivan shoots a fifth series of 105.1 , her second lowest score in a series, and is currently placed at sixth spot. The Indian needs to hold her composure and should not drop below 632.6 to have a chance to get into the eight-shooter final.

Suchika Tariyal confirms India's first medal at Asian Games 2026 after she enters semis of women's traditional 60kg in MMA event. The 36-year-old Tariyal will compete in the semifinal on 21 September.
Suchika defeated Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa in the quarter-finals!

Read Mihir Vasavda's profile of Suchika, who, he writes, started pursuing martial arts as a means to protect herself, and after dabbling, and winning, in various disciplines, she came to MMA. She also appeared on MTV Roadies and later India’s Ultimate Warrior
Here's a quick bio of Sucharika (via Sports Authority of India):

A native of Rohtak, Haryana, Sucharika comes from a modest and conservative family background. Her sporting journey began at the age of 12 after an incident of eve-teasing, which motivated her to take up judo as a means of self-defence. She initially trained at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and subsequently at the Dada Dev Mandir Centre in Palam, further honing her skills at SAI Bhopal. Pursuing competitive sport required her to overcome family reservations, particularly concerning the challenges faced by girls travelling for competitions. She subsequently established herself as an international-level judoka, representing India in more than 20 international Judo competitions.

Suchika went on to become an eight-time National Judo Champion and secured several major international medals for India. She won Gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games, besides winning Silver at the 2018 Commonwealth Judo Championships. She also represented India at multiple Asian Judo Championships. At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, she competed in the Women’s -57 kg category and narrowly missed a podium finish, gaining valuable experience at the highest level of international Judo. She subsequently expanded her career into Ju-Jitsu, achieving a major milestone in 2024 by winning Gold in the Adults Ju-Jitsu Contact Female -63 kg category at the JJIF Ju-Jitsu World Championships. Her success across Judo and Ju-Jitsu provided a strong foundation for her transition into MMA.

Suchika made her MMA debut in 2017 with a victory, before taking a seven-year break from the sport while continuing to compete successfully in Judo and Ju-Jitsu. In November 2024, she signed a multi-fight contract with BRAVE Combat Federation in the Women’s Strawweight division. She returned to professional MMA at BRAVE CF 92 in Bahrain in December 2024, securing a victory. Alongside her sporting career, Suchika was appointed as a Head Constable in CISF and subsequently joined the Department of Sports, Haryana as a Junior Coach. Her progression from an accomplished international judoka to a Ju-Jitsu World Champion and professional MMA fighter, coupled with her two medals at the Asian MMA Championship, reflects a distinctive and highly successful multi-discipline combat-sport career. Her extensive international experience, championship credentials and continued progression in MMA position her as an athlete with strong potential to bring further laurels to the nation.
As it was expected in hockey, India has crossed the double digit score against Uzbekistan with striker Deepika scoring six goals alone.

In the second relay of shooting qualification, Elavenil Valarivan is on fire at the moment. After an okay first series of 105.4, Ela scored 106.3 in the second series and improved it to 106.6 in the third series.
Three more series to go but Ela has put India in a strong position for the team medal.

India are absolutely putting Uzbekistan to the sword here at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium. With seven minutes left for the third quarter to end, India have banged in 11 goals. Six of those have come from the designated dragflicker Deepika's stick!
The Uzbek keeper looks like she cannot wait for this misery to get over!
Rishabh Das enters swimming final, Utkarsh Patil ends 12th

Rishabh Das qualified for the final of the men's 100m breaststroke event after finishing fifth overall in the heats with a time of 54.85 seconds. China's Xi Jiayu, the Asian record holder, topped the heats, while Japan's Hidekazu Takehara finished second. Das was 0.63 seconds behind Takehara. India's Utkarsh Patil finished 12th in the qualification round. Das will compete in the final on Sunday afternoon.
INDIA LEAD 8-0 AGAINST UZBEKISTAN IN GROUP STAGE GAME WITH 5 MINS LEFT FOR HALF-TIME

It has been a goal fest for India in the women's hockey game. But interestingly, out of eight goals till now, only two are from penalty corner. The reason behind is the Uzbekistan goalkeeper Rushana Chorieva.

The 18-year-old figured out Navneet's tendency of going to the right and finding out an angle. She made four saves by blocking that angle before Deepika brought her drag flick to breach Rushana via penalty corner.

It was not meant to be as the Indian duo lost 6-12 with Quimcy struggling with her back. The crowd appreciates the Indian duo for their fight. However, beyond anything else, this is a watershed moment for the sport that has just 180 players in the country.

Quimcy Dsouza and her exploits at the Asian Games are going to give more visibility to the sport and India can certainly expect a lot more players picking up the sport. It will be interesting to see if the sport picks up after all the hype or remains the follow once in four years kind of sport.

Quimcy in a lot of pain at the moment, and grimacing every few minutes. Eventually, the Indians lose the second set too. This means in the span of just over a hour, Quimcy has endured a double heartbreak besides picking up a lower back injury.

Last time in the Asian Games, China had won the team gold in the women’s 10m air rifle event with a cumulative score of 1896.6 while the India had won the team silver with a cumulative score of 1886 points.

As of now China stands at the top in terms of team score in the women’s 10m air rifle event with the first 29 shooters shooting. Indivodual scores of each shooter from a country are costed in the team format. The top four spots in the team event with cumulative scores of two shooters are currently occupied by China (1270.6) followed by Korea (1268.2), India (1265.5) and Japan (1264.5). It’s a tense fight for the medals. 16-year-old Chinese Du Yechen, who won the ISSF World Cup title in Hangzhou earlier this year, is yet to shoot with Indian Elavenil Valarivan too shooting in the second batch. Korean Cho Eun-byeo and world number four Misaki Nobata of Japan too are yet to shoot in the second batch.

Meanwhile, the Indian women's hockey team have taken a 2-0 lead at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium with just 8 minutes gone against Uzbekistan in a Pool B game, thanks to goals from from Lalremsiami and Deepika!
Pritish Raj adds: They are already 2-0 up and it will be interesting to see if it becomes a double digit scoreline by the end of the match.

We have an injury break in the mixed doubles bronze medal playoff as Quimcy is getting some help from the physio on her lower back. The injury break is being extended for Quimcy, who has looked in trouble from the first set which the Indian pair lost.
"I can try, I can try," we overhear Quimcy tell her coaches.

An anti-climactic finish in the mixed doubles bronze medal match between Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza and Mohd Anas Imran Beg vs Minh Tan Nguyen & Gia Nghi Trinh (Vietnam) as the Indian duo loses the first set 9-12. The doubles look far more thrilling but Anas needs to work on his reception of the service as they lost four points there. Quimcy is at her usual game, some flawless shot making but some poor serves.

From Nagoya, Mihir Vasavda writes: India’s chances of a team medal will rest heavily on Elavenil Valarivan. Sonam Maskar has finished second behind Wang Zifei of China with a total of 634.1. Vidarsa Vinod is ninth with 630.4 - she is out of reckoning for individual final. Sonam will drop to third provisionally after South Korea’s Hyojin Ban finishes with 634.9

Quimcy Dsouza loses the bronze medal and a lot of it goes down to her composure. Like her semifinal, she was leading 10-7 in the second game but gave away four consecutive points and lost 12-11 in the second game. Coincidentally, she had defeated Sakamoto in the group stage match but couldn't repeat it this time. Fourth place finish for the girl from Mumbai.
Quimcy is distraught but she doesn't have time to grieve right now. Mixed doubles bronze match starts soon and she has an immediate chance at redemption

Quimcy relinquishes lead of the second set at the worst time possible. She goes from 10-8 up to 11-10 down as Sakamoto reaches match point. And the Indians take a time out. Just before that, with the scores at 10-10, the Japanese thought she had won another point, but Quimcy appealed and then got the point reversed for the ball hitting the edge.
But finally, Quimcy loses the second set to finish fourth!
Quimcy has managed to stay in the lead all through the second set after losing the first. The Japanesefans are rallying behind Sakamoto.
Pritish Raj writes: Quimcy needs to keep her calm. She gave away two easy points to Sakamoto and the experienced Japanese have made it 6-6 in the second set.

In case you are checking out teqball for the first time, here's what the sport looks like. A table like the one used in table tennis, albeit curved. And players playing like you would foot volley. You can serve with your head or your foot.

Meanwhile, Pritish Raj adds: If you're wondering why few points are being replayed in Quimcy's match, it is because they are rubbing the edge. If the ball goes of the edge, then it's called edge ball and the point is replayed.

Quimcy Dsouza is facing the home favourite Yuina Sakamoto of Japan in the bronze medal match and it is not an easy feat to do that. It was a thrilling final few points in the first game and Sakamoto uses her experience to win the set 12-11.
Mihir Vasavda, The Indian Express' man on the ground in Nagoya for these Asian Games, sends us this update:
Sonam has moved to second at half way stage of her series. Consistent scores of 10.6-10.8 in the third series, with 10.5 being the lowest.
Mihir Vasavda, The Indian Express' man on the ground in Nagoya for these Asian Games, sends us this update:
The qualification for 10m women’s air rifle has started. Sonam is fourth and Vidisha sixth in the second series — top eight go to the final. Elavenil yet to start.
Sonam Maskar (below) has a total of 232.4. She is into her third series.
Teqball arena is getting ready for the medal matches while the Indian shooters Vidarsa Vinod and Sonam Maskar are underway at the shooting range in women's 10m Air Rifle qualification.
Experienced shooter Elavenil Valarivan will start her qualification in the next batch as 29 shooters are firing right now.
We have our first sighting of Suraj Singh Mayanglambam! he is the 17th athlete to compete on Sunday morning in a field of 21. And he's ranked eighth in the men's changquan event.
Update: Suraj gets pushed down to 11th spot after all 21 athletes have had their say.
The score to beat is of Chi Hin Kuong (9.723). The Macao athlete is followed by compatriot Chi Kuan Song (9.720) and Indonesia's Seraf Naro Siregar (9.720).

Far from the shooting arenas, wrestling mats, and track and field, it is the arena with a curved table and a football that might deliver India’s first medal at the Asian Games. The sport is Teqball, making its debut at the continental showpiece.

With Quimcy Dsouza in the women’s singles bronze medal match, and the pair of Quimcy and Md Anas in the mixed doubles bronze medal match, it is highly likely that India will open its medal count in Aichi-Nagoya with a Teqball medal.
And read this piece on Quimcy Dsouza from Mihir Vasavda, The Indian Express' man on the ground in Nagoya for the Asian Games
Later today, the women's cricket team will compete in the semi-finals at the Asian Games. meanwhile, the men's team flew out to Japan a short while back from the IGI Airport.

We have Suraj Singh Mayanglambam in action in Men's Changquan in wushu to start us off! Suraj is competing in a 21-man field.
Before we get to what's happening with Suraj, here's a quick guide to wushu:

Wushu, sometimes referred to as kung-fu, is the term for the martial art practices that originated and were developed in China. As a sport, wushu is categorized into two main categories, namely Taolu (Routines Competition) and Sanda (Free-Fighting Competition).
Sanda looks something like boxing and MMA, with two combatants going head-to-head, while taolu looks something like gymnastics with weapons where combatants fight... well, imaginary enemies.
Taolu is where Suraj Singh Mayanglambam will be in action. At official World Wushu Championships, the main taolu event categories include:

Good morning sports fans! Welcome to our live coverage of Day 2 at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya! Well it's day 2 only technically, but it's day 1 for India's medal ambitions at Nagoya!

If you’re reading this with a cup of chai in one hand and half-open eyes, congratulations—you’ve woken up just in time for the chaos, the drama (hopefully not much), and potentially India’s very first medal of the Asian Games 2026.

Brew some more coffee, cause the Games comes thick and fast today with wushu, teqball, shooting, badminton, and table tennis action coming up. and there's some cricket too early in the day! it's going to be one heck of a ride! Strap on!
Far from the shooting arenas, wrestling mats, and track and field, it is the arena with a curved table and a football that might deliver India’s first medal at the Asian Games.
The sport is Teqball, making its debut at the continental showpiece.

With Quimcy Dsouza in the women’s singles bronze medal match, and the pair of Quimcy and Md Anas in the mixed doubles bronze medal match, it is highly likely that India will open its medal count in Aichi-Nagoya with a Teqball medal.
